To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Medicare billing data are a useful tool for measuring use of standard first-line chemotherapy regimens in elderly Medicare beneficiaries, but the accuracy of these data varies by treatment regimen and setting of care.
the sensitivity of Medicare claims for documenting treatment of elderly cancer patients with multi-agent regimens is high.

we correctly identified at least three-quarters of elderly Medicare patients treated on a CALGB trial with standard first line multi-agent chemotherapy regimens in ambulatory setting by coding algorithms to their claims data.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing and validating a method to use Medicare claims data to identify Medicare beneficiaries who have been treated with standard first-line chemotherapy regimens for breast, colorectal and lung cancer.
the accuracy of Medicare billing data for identifying patients who receive common multiagent chemotherapy treatments in the ambulatory cancer setting.
the development and evaluation of algorithms to identify patients treated with common multiagent chemotherapy in Medicare data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Medicare claims data can be used to identify elderly cancer patients who receive multi-agent chemotherapy in the ambulatory care setting.
the sensitivity of Medicare billing data is 78% (95% CI, 73% to 83%) for measuring use of standard multiagent chemotherapies in the ambulatory care setting.

the sensitivity of CMS claims data for identifying elderly patients with cancer who receive chemotherapy is 92% (95% CI, 89%–95%) and that the sensitivity for identifying patients who receive the correct multiagent chemotherapy regiments (all drugs billed on the same date) is 78% (95%CI, 74%–82%).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Medicare claims are a reasonable source of data for identifying elderly cancer patients treated with standard first-line chemotherapy in the ambulatory care setting.
the sensitivity for Medicare billing data to document receipt of multiagent chemotherapy regiments is 78%, and the accuracy for the individual regimens ranges between 76% and 83%.
we found that CMS billing claims can be used to identify patients treated with chemotherapy, but the accuracy is low for identifying the correct drugs and dosages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CMS Medicare claims data can be used as a reliable source for identifying patients who received standard chemotherapy regimens in clinical practice.
Medicare claims data can be useful in identifying Medicare patients for comparative effectiveness studies.
Medicare claims data can be used to identify cohorts of patients for comparative effectiveness research.
